author: ValWood
body: I noticed that pombe trm1 is picking up annotation to GO:0160103 | tRNA (guanine(26)-N2/guanine(27)-N2)-dimethyltransferase activity from ARBA This seemed odd is this is fairly well characterized in pombe. CHAt-GPT says Q Is there a version of Trm1 specific only for G26 or that modifies both 26 and 27? • Most characterized Trm1 enzymes are primarily responsible for methylation at G26. • However, there is some evidence (especially from bacterial or archaeal systems) that Trm1-like enzymes can also methylate G27, but this is not universal. • In Saccharomyces cerevisiae (budding yeast) and humans, the Trm1 homologs are mostly described as modifying only G26. • When G27 methylation occurs, it may be due to a different methyltransferase or a bifunctional Trm1, but this is rare and less well characterized. • Some species may have isoforms or paralogs with slightly different specificities, but no widely recognized version is strictly exclusive to G27 or that modifies both with equal efficiency. | Organism/Enzyme | Modification Specificity | Notes | |-----------------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------| | Yeast Trm1 | Primarily G26 | Canonical and best characterized activity | | Human TRMT1 | Primarily G26 | Similar specificity as yeast | | Some bacterial/archaeal Trm1-like enzymes | Possibly G26 and G27 | Less common, needs more study | Final take: • The canonical Trm1 enzyme is specific for guanine 26. • Modification of guanine 27 by Trm1 or related enzymes is not a common or well-established activity. Which aligned with my expectations. Digging a little deeper: There are only 3 EXP annotations to GO:0160103 | tRNA (guanine(26)-N2/guanine(27)-N2)-dimethyltransferase activity The 2 SGD annotations are from the same paper PMID:9801306 https://europepmc.org/backend/ptpmcrender.fcgi?accid=PMC147968&blobtype=pdf This paper doesn't mention G27? https://europepmc.org/backend/ptpmcrender.fcgi?accid=PMC147968&blobtype=pdf Actions and Questions 1. FIX SGD annotation ? @edwong57 2. Is this term required ( maybe for bacteria?) add a taxon restriction if there is not evidence for G27 in eukaryotes 3. I thought ARBA required 5 independent EXP annotations to create rules, is that incorrect @Antonialock * * **ARBA rule (ID and label):** ARBA00088072 * **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC25D12.05 * **Description of issue**
title: SGD annotation and ARBA propagation ARBA00088072 GO:0160103 | tRNA (guanine(26)-N2/guanine(27)-N2)-dimethyltransferase
